clue.text: Staying terribly dark and gloomy

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters of the word before are badly treated and thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone finds a stay somewhere grim and depressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' rearranges STAYING; it looks like an intensifier for 'dark'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stygian, from the river Styx of the underworld, describes deep murky darkness and gloom.

clue.text: Paddy has a wash

parts.note: paddy is British slang for a fit of temper
taken as written

explanation.surface: An Irishman named Paddy takes a bath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paddy' looks like an Irish name but means a tantrum, TEMPER; 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempera is a painting medium, a thin wash of pigment bound with egg yolk.

clue.text: One repeatedly after information found in Arabian tales

indicators.note: after puts the repeated one following the information in the answer

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: repeatedly signals that the letter for one appears twice over

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A single fact chased again and again turns up in the Arabian Nights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' and 'repeatedly' are the indicators; GEN is everyday British slang for information, as in 'get the gen'.
explanation.definitionFit: Genii, or jinn, are the spirits that grant wishes in the Arabian Nights tales.

clue.text: Any girl so mistreated might react thus

indicators.note: so mistreated says the letters of the words before are abused into another order

explanation.surface: Any young woman treated badly would respond with fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so mistreated' rearranges ANY GIRL, and the definition says how such a girl would react.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone badly treated would naturally respond in a cross and furious manner.

clue.text: Wild, wild Wales in the 50s

indicators.note: in places the rearranged country's letters between the two fifties

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, so fifties plural are L and another, written LS

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters of the following country run riot and land in a new order

explanation.surface: A nostalgic look at a rowdy Welsh scene in the 1950s.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' (the second one) and 'in' are the indicators; the 1950s are a red herring, as '50s' is read as two Roman fifties.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawless people or places are wild and untamed, with no rules obeyed.

clue.text: Time to admit pig on a bus?

indicators.note: to admit means to let in, so the time period takes the animal inside

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, marks a time era
a boar is a male pig

explanation.surface: A conductor wonders whether a pig may be let onto a bus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to admit' is the container signal; the question mark marks the definition as an example, being on a bus being one way to be on board.
explanation.definitionFit: Being aboard a vehicle means being on it, as a bus passenger.

clue.text: Beggars description in Naples

parts.note: reads as how one might describe beggars, but it is the very word Neapolitans used for their street beggars

explanation.surface: How the poor of an Italian city are described.
explanation.definitionFit: Lazzaroni was the name for the homeless poor and beggars of Naples.

clue.text: Striking entails disruption

indicators.note: disruption means the letters of the word before are broken up and set in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A dramatic industrial dispute brings disruption.
explanation.definitionFit: A salient feature is striking or prominent, standing out from the rest.

clue.text: Result of choosing the wrong type for the job?

definitions.text: Result of choosing the wrong type for the job?

parts.words: Result of choosing the wrong type for the job?
parts.note: reads as hiring the wrong kind of person for a post, but type is printing type set by hand

explanation.surface: A bad hiring decision has consequences.
explanation.definitionFit: A typesetter picking the wrong piece of metal type produces a misprint in the text.

clue.text: Sign on to tour the Middle East

indicators.note: to tour means to travel around, so the first word wraps round the region

parts.note: taken as written
ME is the standard abbreviation for the Middle East

explanation.surface: A traveller hopes for a good sign before a trip around the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to tour' is the container signal; the surface makes it sound like a trip abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen is a sign or portent of something to come.

clue.text: Awful woman novelist has blue veins

parts.note: a gorgon is a fearsome, ugly woman, after the snake-haired monsters of myth
Emile Zola was the French novelist of Germinal and Therese Raquin

explanation.surface: A terrible woman writer is shown to have varicose veins.
explanation.definitionFit: This Italian cheese is famous for the blue mould veins running through it.

clue.text: Twins have empty garage, acquiring car

indicators.note: an empty garage keeps only its first and last letters, its middle cleared out

parts.note: the Mini is a famous small British car

explanation.surface: Two siblings share an empty garage until they buy a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' leaves G and E of 'garage'; 'acquiring' adds the MINI.
explanation.definitionFit: Gemini, the zodiac sign and constellation, is represented by the twins Castor and Pollux.

clue.text: Gives information which could lead to making an arrest

indicators.note: could lead to making signals that the following letters may be remade into something else

explanation.surface: A police informer tells all, hoping it ends in someone being arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could lead to making' rearranges AN ARREST; 'which' is a link. The police surface hides the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: To narrate is to tell a story or give an account of events.

clue.text: It may catch one in the act

definitions.text: It may catch one in the act

parts.words: It may catch one in the act
parts.note: sounds like catching a criminal red-handed, but the act is a circus performance and the catching is of a falling acrobat

explanation.surface: Something that catches a wrongdoer red-handed.
explanation.definitionFit: A circus trapeze act has a net slung beneath to catch any performer who falls.

clue.text: Watch parts required for telescopes?

parts.note: watch parts suggests the innards of a timepiece, but here watch is a verb: the parts you look through

explanation.surface: A horologist needs components for some optical instruments.
explanation.definitionFit: The lens a viewer puts the eye to on a telescope or microscope is called this.

clue.text: The price of a suit

parts.note: reads as what a tailored outfit ..., but the suit is a lawsuit, and the legal expenses awarded are this

explanation.surface: What a new suit of clothes sets you back.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, costs are the expenses of a court case that the losing party may be ordered to pay.

clue.text: He splits a couple of poles made of wood

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: splits means the following pair is broken apart by the first word pushed in

parts.note: the earth's two poles are South and North, S and N
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man chopping wood splits a pair of poles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'splits' is the container signal; 'poles' suggests wooden posts, which fits the wood surface, but means the compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashen can mean made from the timber of the ash tree, as well as pale grey.

clue.text: Elegant French female

parts.note: reads as describing a chic Frenchwoman, but it is the French adjective for well-groomed in its feminine form

explanation.surface: A stylish woman from France.
explanation.definitionFit: Soignee is a French adjective, here with its feminine ending, meaning well groomed and elegant.

clue.text: Not a partner to go around with

definitions.meaning: in a firm, an ... is a member of staff ranked below the partners
to keep company or mix socially with someone

explanation.surface: A junior employee told whom to spend time with.
explanation.definitionFit: Associate names both a junior colleague below partner level and the verb for keeping company with others.

clue.text: Not much spoken about, as space travel can be

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the spoken word goes round the small amount

parts.note: oral means spoken rather than written
a bit is a small amount, not much

explanation.surface: Space travel is rarely discussed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal; 'Not much spoken about' reads naturally as one phrase, but splits into three jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: Space travel that circles a planet in orbit is described as orbital.

clue.text: Metal cover for the sewer

parts.note: suggests a manhole cover over a drain, but the sewer is someone who sews and the cover protects a finger

explanation.surface: A drain cover over the sewers.
explanation.definitionFit: A small metal cap worn on the fingertip protects someone sewing from the needle.

clue.text: Pinches tin-opener, set askew

indicators.note: the opener of a word is its first letter
set means arranged, so the letters of the next word are set in a new order

explanation.surface: A tin-opener nips fingers when it is fitted crooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opener' of 'tin-opener' gives T; 'set' rearranges ASKEW to WEAKS. 'askew' looks like a description, but it is the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To tweak is to pinch and twist sharply, as with a nose or cheek.

clue.text: Very serious internal trouble?

parts.note: reads as a grave medical complaint inside the body, but the internal trouble is within a nation

explanation.surface: A worrying medical complaint inside the body.
explanation.definitionFit: A civil war is armed conflict between groups within the same country, the gravest domestic strife.

clue.text: Put away in a container for the scientist

indicators.note: in places the eaten-up word within the receptacle

parts.note: a bin is a container for rubbish or storage
food put away has been eaten, so it is off the plate; put away also means stowed off

explanation.surface: Instructions to store something in a box for a lab worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal and 'for the' is a link; boffin is British slang for a scientist.
explanation.definitionFit: Boffin is informal British slang for a scientist or technical expert.

clue.text: Fall short of a pound note — forged, perhaps

definitions.text: Fall short of a pound note — forged, perhaps

parts.words: Fall short of a pound note — forged, perhaps
parts.note: a forged banknote fails to be the real thing, so it falls short of a genuine pound note

explanation.surface: A counterfeit note is not worth what it claims.
explanation.definitionFit: A forged banknote is counterfeit, not genuine, the opposite of true.

clue.text: One blow to end a fight in pure slapstick

parts.note: a single blow or rap is a knock
a bout is a boxing match or fight, so a fight is a bout

explanation.surface: A single punch finishes a boxing bout in a comic display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to end' and 'in' are links. Knockout looks likely from 'One blow to end a fight', but the letters split as KNOCK + A BOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Knockabout comedy is rough, boisterous slapstick humour.

clue.text: The object of some ear-piercing work

definitions.text: The object of some ear-piercing work

parts.words: The object of some ear-piercing work
parts.note: ear-piercing suggests a shrill noise, but it is literal: the fleshy part of the ear pierced for earrings

explanation.surface: Something deafeningly loud is aimed at someone.
explanation.definitionFit: The earlobe is the soft lower part of the ear usually pierced for earrings.

clue.text: Keep on being saucy about half-sister

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the cheeky word goes round the sibling's half

parts.note: pert means impudent or saucy

indicators.note: half signals taking just the first three letters of the following six-letter word

explanation.surface: A girl keeps on being cheeky to her half-sister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' and 'about' are the indicators, and 'being' is a link; 'half-sister' looks like a relation but is split into signal and fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To persist is to keep on or continue steadfastly.

clue.text: Declared a supporter in possible deal

indicators.note: in places the limb within the rearranged letters
possible hints at one possible arrangement of the following word's letters

parts.note: a leg supports the body or a table, so it is a supporter

explanation.surface: Someone announces a backer in a potential business deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possible' and 'in' are the indicators, and 'a' is a link; the anagram of the deal word comes out as ALED.
explanation.definitionFit: Alleged means claimed or asserted, as yet without proof.
